# Scenario concepts -- brainstorm

**Design file (WHAT).** Ideas are discussed and decided here. How they are built -- the turning-point model, the reused
WL mechanics, the faction template, the status per slot -- is in `TIMELINES.md`; the order of the work in
`../TODO.md`. Nothing here implies code changes by itself.

**The flow lives in `timeline-overview.drawio`** (generated by `tools/shattered-legacies/timelines/timeline_overview_gen.py`
-- edit the generator, not the drawio). This file holds the reasons, lore and details behind each box. Decision IDs
(D1 ... D17) are the same in both.

Status: everything below is **agreed** unless marked *open*.

---

## 1. Vocabulary

| Term              | Meaning                                                                                                 |
|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Timeline          | umbrella for all of this: any deviation from WL's default history (folder `ShatteredLegacies/Timelines/`) |
| Pick              | a start choice in WL's pick dialog (`FactionChoiceDialogSetup`)                                          |
| Fallback          | second start when the HQ falls                                                                          |
| Sub path          | voluntary commitment to another direction while the faction still stands                                |
| Betrayal          | the faction (or one of its leaders) turns on its team or allies                                         |
| Turning point     | taking a fallback / sub path / betrayal -- from the Hourglass (humans) or by code (bots, forced)        |
| Hourglass of Fate | the trigger building (`nZh0`, 0.53); one research per turning point, greyed out until its trigger fired; WL's own turning-point researches (Scarlet Crusade) are listed too. Sudden death shatters it |
| Full / light      | a full turning point swaps the faction (like WL's Scarlet Crusade); a light one keeps it and changes it (name, object limits, a few additions) -- `TIMELINES.md` section 1 |
| Rogue nation      | a faction forced out of its team while it still stands; own team, hostile to all                        |
| Shared box        | one goal several factions race for; the first one closes it (World Tree, Helm of Domination)            |
| End goal          | a faction's final quest (crown in the drawio); some change alliances                                    |
| Defection         | the human switches to a new faction; the old faction moves to a free slot as a bot                      |
| Arthas game / Garithos game | the two outcomes of Lordaeron's pick (D1)                                                     |

Alliance terms: **Great Alliance** = the starting alliance in Arthas games. **North / South Alliance** = what is left
after it breaks (and the start teams in Garithos games). **Empire of Mankind** = Garithos' empire.

---

## 2. Ground rules

- **Scope cap per slot**: fallback, plus at most 1 sub path, 1 betrayal, 1 pick. A sub path may also be the betrayal.
- **Lore test**: every concept names a lore anchor and one divergence.
- **One fallback per faction; team changes at most once.** Approved exceptions: rogue Quel'thalas (North -> rogue -> Kalimdor / South), Forsaken (puppet -> free), South factions joining the Empire of Mankind, evil fallbacks that join the victor after an earlier betrayal.
- **Living target**: an option to join team X only appears while team X has a member.
- **Successors keep their player's colour.** A new colour is only needed when one player produces two factions at once (defection).
- **Punishment is a feature**: betrayals and early commitments carry real costs -- that is also the abuse protection.
- **Defeat (fork rule)**: leavers are taken over by bots; the only way to lose is having no CP at all for more than
  5 turns (1 CP is enough to live); losing the essential legends does not defeat a faction. A faction with an
  unused fallback is never defeated -- the fallback runs instead (`TIMELINES.md` section 4).
- **Recycle, then adjust**: successors reuse objects of the main map, the 24p map and stock WC3 assets (content index,
  `../TODO.md`); no new assets.
- **Fallback vs betrayal of the same faction must clearly differ** (team, start size, heroes, what is left behind).

### Bot rules

1. Bots decide at random -- humans can't predict or abuse them.
2. Bots decide the moment a path appears.
3. Single-option paths (betrayals, secession): one roll -- take or never.
4. Picks are decided at the start only.

Deterministic exceptions based on world state are allowed where a random choice would be absurd (D9, D14).

## 5. Shared mechanics

| Hourglass turning points  | all                                             | the Hourglass of Fate (`nZh0`, 0.53): one research per turning point, greyed out until available |
| Pick                      | D1 (new), Dalaran / Gilneas, Sentinels / Draenei, Frostwolf / Warsong | WL's pick dialog                                          |
| Choice at fallback        | Jaina (D6), South fallbacks (D9)                | dialog when the fallback triggers                                                         |
| Tax task                  | Imperial Tax (South -> North), Legion's Tithe (Scourge -> Legion) | every second X % of the payer's income (CP + `PlayerData.TotalIncome` + bot strength-vote bonus) to the recipient(s), never below 0 gold |
| Defection                 | D3 (Forsaken)                                   | WC3 can't move humans between slots: the human keeps the slot and gets the new faction; the old faction moves to a free slot (P11 -> P14 -> P20) as a bot. [ai] check whether `PlayerDistributor` helps |
| Shared box                | World Tree, Helm of Domination                  | first claimant closes it                                                                  |
| Channel                   | World Tree (Archimonde, Garithos, Xal'atath), Argus portal | WL's existing channel mechanic (Archimonde at the tree)                        |
| Inheritance               | every fallback, sub path, betrayal              | see section 6                                                                             |
| Barks                     | Garithos, Quel'thalas                           | one table: event / speaker / line / sound                                                 |

## 6. Inheritance rule (used by the "leave behind" effect, `TIMELINES.md`)

**Left behind** = everything the player owns outside the new start area at the moment of the turning point, minus what the concept takes along.

| Step | Outcome             | When                                                                                  | Example                                      |
|------|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| 1    | **Kept**            | the faction stays where it is (team change only)                                      | rogue Quel'thalas, free Scourge, Corrupted Scarlet |
| 2    | **Lore heir**       | the concept names an heir AND the heir is still on the old team                       | Sentinels -> Druids; Dalaran -> Lordaeron    |
| 3    | **Neutral hostile** | everything else (old base becomes a creep camp / neutral capital, like Grim Batol)    | Druids' Kalimdor ruins                       |
| --   | Never by default    | to the enemy that caused the turning point                                            | --                                           |

Heroes listed by the concept go along; others follow the chain. Timing: at the turning point, always before WL's defeat / observer switch.
*Open* [ai]: do neutral-hostile WL capitals still count for other factions' quests?

## 7. Great Alliance (Arthas games only)

- **Start**: North (Lordaeron, Quel'thalas, Dalaran / Gilneas) and South (Stormwind, Ironforge, Kul Tiras) are one team (`TeamSetup.Alliance`), the Thandol rocks are gone, the **Imperial Tax** (South -> North) runs. Garithos games use WL's default North / South teams instead -- no tax, no Defias, no dissolution. The Thandol vote is retired.
- **Lore anchor**: the first Alliance of Lordaeron broke apart over Terenas' levy for the internment camps -- Gilneas, Stromgarde and Quel'thalas refused to pay.
- **Dissolution -- first trigger wins**: D2 tax vote passes · Lordaeron's HQ falls · the Lich King's Ascension · Archimonde consumes the World Tree. Then the Great Alliance becomes the North Alliance, the payers form the South Alliance; every coin paid north bought nothing.
- **D2 tax vote**: human payers decide by majority (one human alone decides; two humans must agree; tie = keep paying), bots abstain; an all-bot South rolls once. Opens at turn 10, can be called again every 5 turns. The North doesn't vote.
- **Defias**: neutral hostile spawns near Stormwind's CPs every X minutes, no XP; stop with the dissolution.

**Announcements** (drafts):

| Event                | Announcement                                                                                                                                       |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| tax vote passes      | "The southern kingdoms refuse to pay another coin for the north. The Great Alliance is no more."                                                   |
| Lordaeron's HQ falls | "The capital of Lordaeron has fallen, and the Great Alliance dies with it. Every coin the South sent north bought nothing but ashes."               |

(Stormwind / Ironforge / Kul Tiras individual lines from earlier drafts can be reused as flavour if the vote shows who voted.)

## 8. Slots

### P10 Lordaeron -- pick D1: Arthas or Garithos

**Arthas games** (WL as is, plus the Great Alliance):
- WL's **"The Culling"**: Stratholme falls and "Line of Succession" is not done -> Arthas joins the Scourge.
- WL's **"Line of Succession"** (Arthas lvl 10 + Howling Fjord): King Arthas, can't permanently die. End goal: **Kingdom of Man** (WL).
- **Scarlet Crusade** = WL's research restart at Tyr's Hand (D14). Hero Saidan Dathrohan -- the man Balnazzar impersonates.
- Lordaeron's HQ falling breaks the Great Alliance.

**Garithos games** (meme, reference: Executor N'ral's playlist "Garithos Takes Over the Human Campaign"):
- **Lore anchor**: Grand Marshal Othmar Garithos, last commander of Lordaeron's resistance, xenophobic ("The only good non-human is a dead non-human."), arrested Kael's elves for treason. His army: humans and dwarves.
- **Divergence**: Terenas keeps Arthas at court and gives the plague to the Grand Marshal.
- **No fallback** -- the gamble. No Scarlet Crusade can exist, so the Legion never gets its puppet (Garithos' people are nobody's puppet).
- Garithos = main hero, buffed. Not Valiance Expedition's second hero in this game. Detheroc cannot be revived (his death freed Garithos' men in *Dreadlord's Fall*).
- **The campaign chain**:
  1. **Shores of Northrend** (reuses WL's quest): Mal'Ganis slain, Frostmourne refused (bark).
  2. **The Well of Eternity**: Garithos channels at the World Tree (shared box) -> empowered.
  3. **Empowered Garithos reaches Northrend** -> the **Empire of Mankind** forms: every human and dwarven faction of North and South joins (dwarves stay in his army). End goal crown. Announcement: "The kingdoms of men and dwarves kneel to the first Emperor of Mankind. The elves are not invited."
  4. **Victor over the Scourge** -> claims the Helm of Domination (shared box) -> **D11 wear or shatter**: wear = Lich King Garithos, undead serve the Empire (Ebon Blade: "Technically human."); shatter = all Scourge undead die, the free Forsaken survive.
- **D10 Treason!** (Lordaeron lost > 2 CPs -- the elves clearly didn't help enough; bots always): Quel'thalas becomes a rogue nation, no compensation. Also fires when the Empire forms.
- **The Coronation**: capital lost and retaken -> King Arthas is crowned and fights murlocs forever (invulnerable, nobody dies). Once Lordaeron is eliminated he becomes attackable; if the Scourge kills him, it gets Arthas.
- **Barks**: "The only good non-human is a dead non-human." (faction eliminated, verified) · "Die, mongrel!" (enemy hero dies near Garithos, *open*: source) · "Garithos... I'm starting to hate that man." (Kael, when Treason fires, real TFT line).
- Gilneas in the Empire: "Imperial Hounds" announcement -- man's best friend, on a very short leash.

### P3 Quel'thalas

- **D3 Keep or defect** -- when Sylvanas is slain by the Scourge (lore: Arthas killed her and raised her as a banshee).
  - keep: the Scourge gets Sylvanas as a banshee hero.
  - defect: the human plays the **Forsaken** in P3 (Lavender) as an enslaved puppet on the Scourge's team; Quel'thalas moves to a free slot as a bot (Teal).
  - 0.54 (maintainer): Sylvanas is lost to Quel'thalas either way. Bots always defect (one player becomes two). No time window: the decision stays open. The Forsaken start in Northrend near Drak'Tharon (2968, 17655; safe, not lore) with Sylvanas as a banshee hero, an altar and builders, and grow quest by quest into a full faction; breaking free (D4) turns her into the Dark Ranger and frees more of the tech tree; the last quest takes Lordaeron City as Undercity.
- **Fallback: Sunfury** (HQ: Silvermoon Palace lost -- 0.53, maintainer): Kael leads the survivors to Netherstorm. Team: Outland while the Black Citadel stands under the Illidari, then the Horde, otherwise own team (lore: the blood elves joined the Horde after Illidan).
- **Garithos games -- rogue nation** after Treason: **D16** join the night elves (Kalimdor, any time -- the Highborne come home after ten thousand years) or the South (once Lordaeron is gone; bark "Selama ashal'anore!").

**Forsaken** (P3 human, Lavender):
- **D4 break free**: from the civil war on (lore: Sylvanas broke free when the Lich King's grip failed, in the Plaguelands civil war). Latest: automatic when Lich King Arthas dies. May also stay with the Scourge.
- Free Forsaken: Horde if it exists, otherwise own team -- meant to be hard. Quest "The Throne of Lordaeron" (take Lordaeron City -> Undercity).

### P8 Dalaran / Gilneas (pick)

- **Fallback: Theramore / Jaina's Sanctum** for both picks (Gilneas has no own fallback). **D6 Jaina's choice** when the Violet Citadel falls:
  - Stay -> North ("Return to Dalaran": retake the Violet Citadel).
  - Pact of Hyjal -> Horde, or Kalimdor if there is no Horde.
  - Daughter of the Sea -> South (if it exists; Kul Tiras is her family).
  - Turncoat -> Legion, Garithos games only ("I swear she is a demon" -- Garithos was right).
- **D7 The Gates Close**: Genn reseals the Greymane Wall (lore: Gilneas stayed sealed while Lordaeron burned) -> Gilneas joins the South, Dalaran is left behind (heir: Lordaeron, else neutral hostile), no fallback. Needs no Great Alliance, the plague and Genn alive.

### P2 Stormwind / P5 Ironforge / P23 Kul Tiras

- **P2 Valiance Expedition** (fallback) and **P5 Dwarven Expedition** (fallback; working title -- the name must differ from Stormwind's expedition): **D9** stay South or go North. Bots: North if Arthas is still loyal, or in Garithos games.
- **Dwarven Expedition**: a base near the Storm Peaks (Northrend), frost dwarves, a new quest at the titan city ("Secrets of Ulduar"). WL's Explorers' League quest of Ironforge goes to Kalimdor -- the Northrend quest is new.
- **Bolvar** (Valiance) is a claimant of the Helm -> end goal Lich King Bolvar. In Garithos games he races his own Emperor for it.
- **P23 Kezan Enterprise** (fallback, own team). End goal: **acquire 20,000 gold** (*open*: confirm the number).
- In Garithos games all three join the Empire of Mankind when it forms.

### P12 Druids

- **Fallback: Dream trees** (Twilight Grove, Seradane) -> South Alliance. Trigger: the World Tree is consumed / Nordrassil falls (same event).

### P19 Sentinels / Draenei (pick)

- **Fallback for both picks: Maiev's Watchers** (Warden's Cage, Shadowmoon; Kalimdor team; small remnant, Tyrande joins the hunt). Quest "The Hunt": take down the Black Citadel; if Illidan is already beaten, hunt the Legion's demon lords instead.
- **Sentinels -- D8 The River** (when Maiev is available): Maiev abandons Tyrande -> Watchers on their own team, bigger start; Tyrande and the Sentinels' holdings go to the Druids if they are still on the Kalimdor team, else neutral hostile.
- **Draenei -- D15 The Triumvirate** (when Velen meets Archimonde): Velen, Kil'jaeden and Archimonde were the eredar triumvirate; this time Velen says yes -> the **Man'ari draenei** join the Legion.
- Announcements: fallback (desperation) "Ashenvale burns, and the Sentinels are no more. With nothing left to defend, Maiev Shadowsong clings to the only duty that remains: the Betrayer must not go free." · The River (vengeance) "Maiev Shadowsong has left Tyrande to the river. Let Ashenvale burn -- for ten thousand years she guarded the Betrayer, and she will not lose him for one more day."

### P1 Frostwolf / Warsong (pick)

- **D12 Found the Horde** when Archimonde dies (lore: after Hyjal the pact ended and Thrall's people went their own way). The Horde team only exists if founded.
- **Fallback: Twilight's Hammer** (orc HQ falls) -> Old Gods team, base Grim Batol (assets exist). It reuses the Dragonmaw assets and the tech / unit / building trees of the 24p map. Lore: Cho'gall's Old God cult, later Deathwing's servants. End goal: **The Hour of Twilight -- Deathwing returns**.

### P4 Scourge

- **D5 Civil war -- "Exile of the Dreadlords"** (from turn 15, bots always): the Scourge breaks from the Legion -> own team.
  - push: the **Legion's Tithe** (tax task, rate grows) ends;
  - pull: the **Ascension is gated** behind the civil war (WL's "The Ascension": Arthas lvl 12 + channel on the Frozen Throne) -> Arthas claims the Helm -> Lich King Arthas (end goal).
  - the civil war also opens D4 (Forsaken) and D13 (Grand Crusader).
- In Garithos games the civil war is possible too (Kel'Thuzad leads); the Ascension then needs Arthas from the Coronation path.
- **Fallback: Knights of the Ebon Blade** when Lich King Arthas dies -> join the victor (death knights who broke free from the Lich King). The Helm is free again.

### P24 Burning Legion

- **HQ**: all Argus CPs; while the Legion controls Archimonde, Archimonde replaces that rule.
- Archimonde can consume the World Tree (shared box; in Arthas games this also breaks the Great Alliance).
- **Fallback: Dreadlord Insurgents** -- same team, crippled, dreadlords revive at a hidden lair until it is destroyed (lore: demons slain outside the Nether return to it).
- **D13 The Grand Crusader** (after the civil war, Arthas games): forces the Scarlet Crusade into the Legion team -- Balnazzar's mask slips.
- **Puppets in the Legion team**: Corrupted Scarlet Crusade, Jaina (turncoat), Man'ari draenei, Fel Horde (if the Legion beats the Illidari).
- **Argus**: the portal is one-way; a non-Legion hero channels at its site to make it two-way (*Beyond the Dark Portal*: the Alliance went through the enemy's own gate).

### P16 Illidari / P7 Fel Horde

- **Illidari** HQ: the Black Citadel. Magtheridon is enslaved by the Illidari.
- **Illidari fallback: the Ashtongue Deathsworn** (0.63, maintainer; a **full** turning point -- a faction of its own,
  not a light one). Akama's redemption arc.
  - **Trigger:** the Black Temple (`o00F`) destroyed. It stays WL's building and is never renamed (other factions'
    quests need it destroyed); where it stood rises the **Temple of the Deathsworn** (the fork's own type,
    indestructible, the Ashtongue's production centre).
  - **Allies -- the conquest rule** (a reusable building block, meant for most evil factions later: they are
    conquered instead of defeated): the Ashtongue belong to the TEAM of whoever destroyed the Black Temple, then of
    whoever holds the Black Temple's CP (`n00I`). The old team's alliances are removed. Anti-abuse: the Ashtongue
    taking the CP themselves changes nothing; a later conquest by another player switches them again.
  - **The sites** (0.64) -- Shattrath, Halaa (the original map's "Halaar" is a typo), Telredor (placed at
    Zangarmarsh), Oshu'gun -- become the Ashtongue's at once, whoever holds them, and indestructible: FEL-TAINTED
    buildings without buttons. Halaa / Shattrath are conquered (WL's capital capture), not destroyed, before; one that
    is gone anyway is built again.
  - **Purification (0.64):** SHATTRATH is the node. Every 8 s it draws up to 50 mana from each own / allied unit within
    1,500 (160 in all -- many units at once, slower; a mana-burn beam to each), +2 per second by itself, while
    Ishanah's Purify (autocast) is on. Its mana pool IS the purification of the current step (no regeneration, its
    maximum = the step's cost). The order: Shattrath 2,000, Halaa 2,400, Telredor 2,400, Oshu'gun 2,600, the temple
    itself 2,600 = 12,000 -> 10 minutes with perfect mana. While mana flows the current site shows the Obsidian
    Statue's replenish at the size of the bubble, a shield bubble (not at Shattrath -- it has its own; gone when the
    step is done) and a ring of healing-light pillars. Each step done: the tainted building becomes the purified one --
    it trains its units and researches its techs (Shattrath: Luminarchs, Vindicators, weapons, armour, the Luminarchs'
    training; Halaa: Elekk Knights; Telredor: Rangari; Oshu'gun: Elementalists and their training). Every site has a
    quest with a map marker.
  - **Ishanah**, High Priestess of the Aldor, stands next to Shattrath: no move ability, invulnerable until Karabor is
    restored; then a free Ishanah (level, skills, items kept) without Purify.
  - **Final goal "Restoring Karabor to the Light"** (the fifth step: the temple itself): the Temple of the Deathsworn
    becomes the Temple of Karabor (trains Xi'ri the naaru), Ishanah is free, the faction is called **Karabor**.
  - **Start:** the Temple of the Deathsworn trains Defenders, Deathsworn and Seers; the Draenei Hut (Illidari) its
    techs; Akama.
  - **Food (0.64):** 30 from the temple, +6 for every Outland CP their team holds.
  - **Gold:** 10 per minute for every Outland CP their team holds -- they profit from defending their allies' land.
  - **Units:** the Illidari's draenei (Akama -- the same unit, levels kept -- Deathsworn, Seers, Draenei Huts) and the
    24p draenei as their own copies (distinct from WL's Exodar). Illidan is gone for good; naga and demons are not
    theirs.
- **Sunfury is no longer the Illidari slot's pick** -- it becomes Quel'thalas' fallback (a full turning point to WL's Sunfury faction).
- If the **Legion** beats the Illidari, Magtheridon is unleashed and the **Fel Horde** joins the Legion. Otherwise the Fel Horde stays where it is.
- **Fel Horde fallback: Mag'har** (orcs of Nagrand who never drank the blood) -> Horde if it exists, otherwise the victor's team.
  Start: Kil'sorrow Fortress (maintainer, 0.63). Gold: a trading post that produces up to 4 traders by itself (60 s
  each) -- attackable, not controllable, on fixed routes out of Outland (2 to Booty Bay, 2 to Fuselight); 4 on the
  road at once completes a quest. Needs a mule / pack-horse asset.

### Old Gods: P9 Skywall / P13 Black Empire / P17 Ahn'qiraj

| Faction      | Fallback (joins the victor)   | Lore                                                                      |
|--------------|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Skywall      | *open*: The Earthen Ring, or Ramkahen | Earthen Ring: shamans who restore the elemental balance once Al'Akir falls |
| Black Empire | *open*: **Xal'atath**, or Titan Watchers | Xal'atath: "Blade of the Black Empire", serves the victor as a weapon, as she served the shadow priests |
| Ahn'qiraj    | Brood of Nozdormu             | the bronze flight that guarded the Scarab Wall                            |

- **D17 The Blade turns** (only if the Black Empire's fallback is Xal'atath -- *open*): Xal'atath can channel at the World Tree too (shared box). Consuming it is her betrayal: she leaves the victor's team for her own. If the World Tree is already gone, she turns when sudden death starts. The Old Gods are never truly beaten.
- Old Gods flavour: they win through other people's falls (Twilight's Hammer, Xal'atath). Later candidates: Emerald Nightmare, Druids of the Flame.

## 11. Sudden death: The End Time (shared quest)

- **Lore anchor**: the Infinite Dragonflight unravels timelines; the bronze flight guards the true one. Shattered Legacies *is* a broken timeline -- the bronze dragons don't care who wins, only that someone does.
- **Trigger**: turn >= X and one of: stalemate; nothing decisive for Y turns; all fallbacks used up.
- **Phases**: Omen (announcement + countdown) -> the sands run out (every Hourglass of Fate shatters, rifts at contested CPs; Xal'atath turns if she hasn't yet) -> resolution (hold the Caverns of Time for N turns, or most CPs when the countdown ends).
- *Open*: X, N, Y.
